items.title: Scientists discover a secret glow in toxic fire salamanders
items.snippet: Researchers have discovered a surprising hidden ability in Europe's familiar black-and-yellow fire salamanders: they glow green and cyan under ultraviolet light. The mysterious fluorescence comes mainly from glands in their skin and their toxic secretions, which can continue glowing for more than 24 hours after being released.

Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden 100-million-year-old volcanic system

The discovery sheds new light on the disappearance of an ancient ocean and the powerful geological forces that reshaped the Middle East.

items.title: Islands harbor nearly 20% of Earth's biodiversity, yet remain overlooked in conservation strategies
